title: Cycling a new tank and client handover
audience: Aquarium maintenance technicians who check a site, cycle and hand over a new or newly set-up tank for a client
learningOutcomes: Explain the nitrogen cycle and why a new tank must be cycled before it carries a full livestock load
Check a new tank site for a level, supported floor, power and water access before any water is added
Run and record a cycle using the owner's plan and the test results, rather than a calendar
Prepare a written handover pack, and price the set-up and cycle work under the approved method
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government, Electrical licences and certificates (last updated 23 June 2026); NSW Government, Plumbing, draining and gasfitting licences (last updated 31 July 2026); Queensland Building and Construction Commission, Building work that needs a QBCC licence (last reviewed and published 16 April 2026).

instruction.heading: What a cycle is
instruction.body: A new filter has few of the bacteria that break down ammonia. One group of bacteria converts ammonia from food and waste to nitrite, and another group converts nitrite to nitrate. Until both groups are established, ammonia and nitrite can build up to toxic levels. A cycle is complete when the test results show it, not when a date passes.

instruction.heading: Check the site before any water goes in
instruction.body: Choose a flat, hard, level site that can carry the filled weight of the tank, the stand and the equipment. A slanted or uneven base can put stress on the glass. Keep the tank out of direct sunlight, away from draughts, doors, windows and high-traffic areas. Confirm there is a suitable power point with a safety switch, that cords can be kept out of the water, and that the water supply is within reach. A filled tank is heavy, so plan the lift and use enough people. Check the tank for leaks at the seams and the base while it is empty and dry, and again during the first fill, and record what you find. This course covers setting up a tank, not building one. Building or modifying a glass tank is outside this course.

instruction.heading: Clean, fill and condition
instruction.body: Wash the substrate in a bucket until the rinse water is clear enough for the plan, because new substrate often clouds the water. Rinse decorations and new filter media in clean water before they go in, and do not use detergents. Fill the tank slowly, using water at about room temperature, and condition it with a product that removes chlorine and chloramine at the dose on its label. Start the heater and the filter as the plan directs, with the heater set in the range for the livestock (see the system types lesson). A cloudiness that persists or worsens is reported.

instruction.heading: Running the cycle
instruction.body: There are two broad approaches: a cycle with fish, which needs close monitoring and a plan for feeding and water changes, and a cycle without fish, which uses an ammonia source to feed the bacteria. The owner and the plan choose the method. Any product used to start the bacteria, and any ammonia source, is used strictly at the label dose and as the plan directs. This course does not set amounts or name products. Test ammonia, nitrite, nitrate and pH at the interval the plan sets, and record every result. Keep the light on a timer, so that algae does not take hold while the tank is young. Overfeeding is a common cause of a spike, so feed the amount the plan sets and remove uneaten food.

instruction.heading: Adding livestock in stages
instruction.body: Do not add livestock until the cycle is complete and the plan agrees. Add livestock in small groups over the period the owner's plan sets, rather than all at once, because a large sudden load can push the bacteria past what they can handle. New livestock must be held in quarantine as the owner's plan directs (see the livestock lesson). Acclimatise each animal by floating its sealed bag in the tank for the period the plan sets, then net the animal out. Do not pour the transport water into the tank. Record each addition with its date, the number of animals and the test results before it.

instruction.heading: The client handover pack
instruction.body: A handover pack lets the owner keep the tank safe after you leave. It should include the tank size and the system type; the equipment list, with each item labelled and each isolation point marked; the maintenance plan (see the routine visit lesson); the test log and the cycle record; the water source and the conditioning method used; the livestock list supplied by the owner; the emergency steps for a power failure, a heater fault or a leak; a list of things that must never be added, such as pool chemicals; and referral contacts for electrical, plumbing and animal health matters. State the limits of your service in writing, and get the owner's sign-off.

instruction.heading: Pricing the set-up and cycle work
instruction.body: Set-up and cycle management is skilled work, and its value comes from the checks, the records and the handover. Price it as a defined scope under the business's approved method. Price the set-up, the test visits during the cycle and the handover pack as separate items, so the client can see what each one covers. Do not absorb test visits as free work. Charge for materials under the materials cost policy. Do not sell animals unless the business is authorised to do so.

procedure: Confirm the work order, the tank's system type, and the owner's plan for the cycle method, the test interval and the livestock.
Check the site for level, support, distance from direct sun and draughts, the power point and the water access.
Check the tank for leaks while it is empty and dry, again during the first fill, and record the result.
Wash the substrate, and rinse decorations and media in clean water without detergent.
Fill slowly, condition the water as the label directs, and start the heater and filter at the setting the plan gives.
Run the cycle using the chosen method, test at the planned interval, and record each result.
Add livestock in stages only after the plan and the test results agree, with quarantine and acclimatisation as the plan directs.
Prepare the handover pack, walk the owner through the isolation points and emergency steps, and record the owner's sign-off.

workedExamples.situation: A client wants fish added the afternoon the tank is set up, so that they can take advantage of a sale at the shop on Saturday.
workedExamples.reasoning: Advise against adding livestock on the day of set-up. The tank has no established biological filter, so ammonia and nitrite can build up. Offer to test the tank through the cycle, and agree a date for livestock once the plan and the results agree. Record the client's request and your advice. Do not add fish to meet a sale date.

workedExamples.situation: During a cycle, the ammonia reads higher than at the last visit. The client has been adding extra food because the fish look hungry.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the extra feeding and remove the uneaten food. Retest with an in-date reagent, and record the result, the feeding change and the time. Check the filter and the heater. Follow the plan for any water change. Do not add a product to force the reading. Record the likely cause as far as it is known, and tell the owner.

equipmentAndPpe: Spirit level or equivalent for the stand and floor check
Dedicated buckets for tank water and substrate washing
Water conditioner that removes chlorine and chloramine, used at the label dose
Test kit or meter, in date, for the cycle
Gloves and footwear with grip, with a team lift arrangement, as set by {{business:safety.required_ppe}}

commonErrors.error: Adding livestock before the cycle is complete.
commonErrors.prevention: Add livestock only when the plan and the test results agree, and add it in stages.

commonErrors.error: Judging the cycle by the calendar.
commonErrors.prevention: Judge the cycle by the test results and the trend.

commonErrors.error: Using tap water without conditioning it.
commonErrors.prevention: Condition all tap water as the label directs.
Give a written pack, and get the owner's sign-off.

commonErrors.error: Doing cycle test visits for free.
commonErrors.prevention: Price cycle monitoring under the approved method.

commonErrors.error: Lifting a filled tank alone, or onto an uneven floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the floor and the stand, plan the lift, and use enough people.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A filled tank is heavy and can fail if the floor or stand is not level and rated.

Installing a new power point, adding fixed lighting, rewiring a controller or connecting a new electrical supply is electrical work. In New South Wales, electrical wiring work, including installing and repairing, is licensed whatever its cost (last updated 23 June 2026). This lesson does not grant electrical authority.

Connecting a new water supply or drain to plumbing is plumbing work. In New South Wales, plumbing, draining and gasfitting work is licensed whatever its cost (last updated 31 July 2026). In Queensland, a QBCC licence is needed for plumbing or drainage work of any value (last reviewed 16 April 2026). This lesson does not grant any plumbing licence.
Selling or supplying live animals may need authority that this course does not grant.
Water from unknown sources, and the discharge of any water at set-up, must follow the route rule in the water conservation lesson.

qualityStandard: The site is checked and recorded before any water goes in
Each cycle test is recorded, and the cycle is judged on the results
No livestock is added until the plan and the results agree, and each addition is recorded
The handover pack is completed and signed off by the owner
documentationEvidence: Site check record with level, support, power and water access
Leak check record for the empty and the filling tank
Cycle test log with each result, time and temperature
Livestock addition record with date, number and test results
summary: A new tank needs a cycle before it carries a full load. Judge the cycle by test results, not by the calendar.
Check the site, the power and the floor before any water goes in, and do not carry out electrical or plumbing work.
Add livestock in stages, after the plan and the results agree.
A written handover pack protects the owner and the business, and cycle monitoring is priced as its own scope.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants livestock added on the day a new tank is set up. What is the correct advice?
options: Add the livestock today, because the sale ends soon and the client will lose the offer if they wait for the results
Add half the livestock today and the rest later with no tests, since the first group will show the tank is ready
Advise against it, and agree a date for livestock once the test results and the owner's plan show the cycle is ready
Add the livestock at night when the tank is quiet, so the animals settle before the owner visits in the morning

knowledgeChecks.question: During a cycle, ammonia reads higher than at the last visit. What is the first step?
options: Add a larger dose of product to bring it down quickly before the fish are affected
Empty the tank and start the cycle again, since the new reading shows the tank is failing
Ignore it because the fish look well and are still feeding normally at each visit today
Stop the extra feeding, remove uneaten food, retest with an in-date reagent, and record the result

knowledgeChecks.question: Which item belongs in a client handover pack?
options: The equipment list with isolation points, the maintenance plan and the emergency steps
The client's personal bank details, so the owner can pay for the next service
Pool chemical instructions for the aquarium, since the same products work for both systems
A promise that the fish will live a long time and that no losses will occur in the tank

officialReferences.title: Electrical licences and certificates
officialReferences.covers: Open the page under When you will need a licence. It defines electrical wiring work to include repairing, says cost makes no difference, and does not mention cleaning or maintenance. Publisher: NSW Government.

officialReferences.title: Plumbing, draining and gasfitting licences
officialReferences.covers: Open the page and check the licence-or-certificate statement for plumbing, draining and gasfitting work. The page lists tanks within plumbing work and does not mention simple hose connections. Publisher: NSW Government.

officialReferences.title: Building work that needs a QBCC licence
officialReferences.covers: Open the page and check the list of building work; plumbing or drainage needs a QBCC licence of any value. The page does not say whether a simple hose connection needs one. Publisher: Queensland Building and Construction Commission (QBCC).

officialReferences.title: electrical licensing outside NSW and whether a given aquarium task is electrical work
officialReferences.covers: Queensland WorkSafe page (no date shown) lists six classes of electrical work licence and states: 'Only an electrical contractor can do electrical work in your home.' It does not mention pumps or heaters. It mentions lights only as street lighting maintenance within linesperson work. Other states, and whether a given aquarium task is electrical work, are not covered by this page. Publisher: WorkSafe Queensland.

officialReferences.title: whether a simple hose fill or a tank's internal plumbing is plumbing work
officialReferences.covers: NSW only: a licence or certificate is needed for any plumbing, draining or gasfitting work regardless of cost, and water plumbing is defined as work connected with the supply or conveyance of water, including tanks. The page does not say whether a simple hose fill is plumbing work, so that point remains unconfirmed. Publisher: NSW Government.
